plate_findings.evidence: A T1-weighted image shows symmetrical hypointense signals in the head of the caudate nucleus and globus pallidus
Hyperintense signals can be observed in the putamen and the head of the caudate nucleus

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Axial T1 MRI at basal ganglia level in 35-year-old molecularly diagnosed neuroferritinopathy patient showing symmetrical hypointensity consistent with basal ganglia iron deposition. b: Axial T2 MRI at basal ganglia level in same neuroferritinopathy patient showing lenticular hypointensity from iron and putaminal/caudate hyperintensity consistent with cavitation/cystic degeneration.
panels.attribution_text: Ohta and Takiyama. MRI findings in neuroferritinopathy.. Neurology research international 2012. doi:10.1155/2012/197438. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Axial section at the level of the basal ganglia in the patient at 35 years of age. (a) A T1-weighted image (TR 400 msec/ TE 14 msec) shows symmetrical hypointense signals in the head of the caudate nucleus and globus pallidus. (b) A T2-weighted image (TR 800 msec/TE 30 msec) shows hypointense changes in the lenticular nucleus. Hyperintense signals can be observed in the putamen and the head of the caudate nucleus.
in_text_mentions: Brain MR images of our case are presented in Figures 1, 2, 3, and 4. Our patient is a 42-year-old Japanese man who first developed hand tremor in his middle teens. He noticed his right foot dragging at age 35, and generalized hypotonia, hyperextensibility, aphonia, micrographia, hyperreflexia, dystonia of his face, and cognitive impairment at age 42. Rigidity, spasticity, and chorea were not observed. His deceased mother had presented similar symptoms. His serum ferritin concentration was apparently low. He was tested by means of the molecular technique and diagnosed as having neuroferritinopa

All images presented here were taken with a 1.5 Tesla MR System. T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and T2*-weighted sequences were collected in the transverse plane. A T1-weighted image is useful for evaluating the atrophy and size of a cyst. As compared with the image at 35 years (Figure 1), that at 42 years demonstrates progression of the cystic formation and deterioration of the cortical atrophy in the frontal lobes (Figures 2(c) and 3(c)). Cortical atrophy can also be seen in the cerebellum (Figure 2(a)). Enlargement of the lateral ventricles is evident (Figure 2(d)).

plate_findings.evidence: symmetrical hypointense signals in the head of the caudate nucleus and globus pallidus
The cystic changes of the lenticular nuclei can be clearly observed. The shape of the cyst is fan shaped

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (a, b, c, d, e). a: T1 pontine section in 42-year-old diagnosed neuroferritinopathy patient; caption states cerebellar cortex atrophy, disease-focused article title supports attribution. Atrophy not in vocabulary so in proposed_findings. b: T1 midbrain section same patient; caption states hypointense change in substantia nigra. Reflects brain iron accumulation but substantia nigra site not in basal ganglia vocabulary term, so in proposed. c: Basal ganglia level shows both vocabulary findings: symmetrical hypointense caudate/pallidal signals extending to putamen and fan-shaped lenticular cystic changes in diagnosed neuroferritinopathy patient. d: Same patient T1 image; caption states enlargement of the lateral ventricles is evident, in-text confirms progression. Not in vocabulary so in proposed_findings. e: Same patient T1 image; caption states cerebral cortical atrophy. Disease attribution supported by panel caption plus disease-focused article title.
panels.attribution_text: Ohta and Takiyama. MRI findings in neuroferritinopathy.. Neurology research international 2012. doi:10.1155/2012/197438. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: T1-weighted images (TR 400 msec/ TE 9 msec) of the same patient at 42 years of age. (a) A cross-section at the pontine level shows cerebellar cortex atrophy. (b) An image of a midbrain section demonstrates the hypointense change in the substantia nigra. (c) An image at the level of the basal ganglia shows symmetrical hypointense signals in the head of the caudate nucleus and globus pallidus. As compared with the findings at 35 years, the hypointense signals in the pallidum extend to the putamen. The cystic changes of the lenticular nuclei can be clearly observed. The shape of the cyst is fan shaped and exactly fits the region of the lenticular nucleus. The cerebral cortex in the frontal lobes is atrophic. The hypointense lesion in the caudate head observed in the image at 35 years of age seems to be combined with the hypointense signal of the anterior horn of the lateral ventricle. (d) In this image, enlargement of the lateral ventricles is evident. (e) This image shows cerebral cortical atrophy.
